title.narrative: Deaf children?s education and communication needs in Burundi

description.narrative: After a 14 year conflict in Burundi which left more than 300,000 people dead and a further 1.2 million people internally displaced or living as refugees, 68% of its population today live in acute poverty. Despite universal education having been introduced, school-aged deaf children and young adults are left out of education policy. Only two sign language interpreters facilitate deaf communications for the whole country, and the only two schools for deaf children use outmoded and incompatible communication methods. This project will study deaf children’s education and communication needs, their access to and achievements in education and the level of deaf awareness in Burundian society. DDP will do library and field research facilitated by Aurora Deaf Aid Africa, (ADAA) in the UK and their contacts in Burundi. It will consult the Burundi National Deaf Association (BNDA), the Centre for Special Needs education, (CNSE) two deaf schools, teachers, Ministry of Education and Social Affairs officers, academics and deaf children and their parents prior to field research and interviews. DDP will then receive feedback from the same participants in a second workshop before producing an in-depth report and recommendations to improve education and communication skills for deaf children and their families.
